conviction_note: The findings sum to -1.1, a mild negative: the FY27 guide is the line that matters. Management's own Q4 run rate ($1.91 x 4 = $7.64) sits about 9% under the one available street FY27 figure ($8.36), with no VA incentives assumed in Q1 FY27. The stock has run about 23% off its early-October low into the print. Against that: a strong Q4 cash walk (leverage 2.0x to 1.7x), an accretive acquisition, the contract-extension read from Leidos, and a name that rallied on a below-street Q4 guide last year. p_up 46 x abs 8.0 gives -0.64. The two measurements agree in sign and are close in size.

The quarter's bar is sourced to a company guide. The FY27 street figure (EPS $8.36, revenue $5.38bn) has ONE source, stockanalysis, with 2 analysts (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mms/forecast/), so the guidance findings are capped small.

expectations.real_bar: After a ~23% run off the October low, the stock needs an FY27 EPS guide at or near the street's ~$8.36 (i.e. some assumed return of VA incentives from January plus Agile accretion) and a clean FY26 cash walk. A guide anchored on the $7.64 Q4 run rate would likely be sold.

next_guide.company_current_guide: none for FY27. CFO: Q4 FY26 (implied adj EPS $1.91, ~13% adj EBITDA margin) is 'a reasonable run rate for earnings power and adjusted EBITDA margin going into next fiscal year'; no incentives assumed in Q1 FY27; formal guidance 'on the year-end call in November' (https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504)
next_guide.basis: The run rate annualises to ~$7.64 against $8.36 street. Closing the gap needs incentives to resume from January under the extended VA contracts, Agile Defense accretion (~$0.15-0.25 if included) and buybacks. Leidos, on the same VA program, called 2027 'not a bottom line growth year' (https://www.webull.com/news/15861762119343104). So the initial guide more likely lands at or below the street than above it.

findings.finding: The CFO said on the Q3 FY26 call that Q4 FY26 (implied adj EPS $1.91 at the midpoint, ~13% adj EBITDA margin) is 'a reasonable run rate ... going into next fiscal year', with no VA MDE incentives in Q1 FY27. Annualised that is ~$7.64, about 9% below the only sourced FY27 street EPS of $8.36 (2 analysts). The initial FY27 guide, due on this call, therefore risks a midpoint below the street unless management assumes incentives resume in January.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is the line this name trades on. Aug 2026: FY EPS guide cut, -7.63%. Feb 2026: revenue guide below street with an EPS raise, -16.51%. May 2026: raise plus $400M buyback, +4.24%. Nov 2025: FY26 revenue guide below street, yet +5.53% (baseline; https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/maximus-stock-rises-56-despite-q4-earnings-missing-estimates).
findings.why_not_priced: The street FY27 number ($8.36, about +4% on FY26) has not been marked to the run rate management gave. If the market priced the run-rate guide, the stock would not have rallied 23% into the print, and the preview would not frame the pause as a possible 'temporary dent'. Capped small because the FY27 bar has one 2-analyst source.
findings.independence: Leidos, on the same VA program, frames its 2027 off a Q4 jumping-off point with no growth (https://www.webull.com/news/15861762119343104; filed separately below as a peer). The Earnings Whispers preview names an extended pause as an FY27 risk (https://finviz.com/news/421257/maximus-faces-va-incentive-pause-test-after-cutting-profit-outlook-as-shares-rally).

findings.finding: Leidos (QTC) is the other large VBA disability-exam vendor under the same incentive pause. On its 2026-11-03 Q3 call it said Health contracted 12% on the VBA business, Q4 is 'a reasonable jumping off point for our 2027 performance', '27 is not a bottom line growth year', and it does not count on more work share. That is a counterparty-adjacent read that the VBA economics are not modelled to rebound in early 2027.
findings.link: Both are prime vendors on VA's Medical Disability Examination program: Maximus via VES (re-awarded Regions 1-4 in Jan 2025), Leidos via QTC (largest share, $5.2bn since 2018). Both face the same VA incentive pause and the same recompete. MDE is Maximus's largest Federal profit driver: the one-quarter incentive removal cut its FY EPS guide by $0.35.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The VA incentive line moved MMS -7.63% in Aug 2026 (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The Leidos call came after Maximus last spoke on fundamentals (Aug 6). MMS still rose over November, so the read-through on 2027 VBA economics does not appear in the price. Leidos's Health segment is small inside a defense-heavy company, so few MMS holders read it.
findings.independence: Shares a theme with the run-rate finding above but comes from a different company's document. Nothing else independent found.

findings.finding: The current VA MDE contracts were due to end 2026-12-31. Leidos said it is 'highly likely our existing contracts will be extended through the first half of 2027' to the VA's planned July 1, 2027 new-contract start, with the award expected April-May 2027. That removes a near-term revenue cliff from Maximus's FY27 guide for three quarters, and the draft RFP 'recognizes the value of demonstrated performance'.
findings.link: Same VA MDE program and contract vehicle as Maximus/VES (see above). The extension is a VA decision that applies to all incumbent vendors.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct precedent. The Jan 2025 MDE re-award was announced outside an earnings window.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: on its Aug call Maximus already flagged a 'likelihood that we could see up to a 6-month extension'. The new information is a second vendor's confirmation and the July 1, 2027 start date, which let Maximus guide three quarters of MDE revenue without a cliff.
findings.independence: Trade press, 2026-11-03: final RFP expected Nov 2026, award Apr-May 2027, start July 1, 2027 (https://samsearch.co/government-contracting-news/vba-disability-exam-recompete-targets-november-rfp-and-2027-start-239915), but it cites Leidos too, so partly the same source.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-19 Maximus agreed to buy Agile Defense for $660M cash (+ up to $50M earnout), closing in Q1 FY27. Agile expects ~$450M calendar-2026 revenue at 12-15% adj EBITDA (~$54-68M, about 10-12x). Pro forma leverage is 2.2-2.3x, inside the 2-3x target. After ~6-6.5% interest on $660M, adjusted EPS accretion (amortisation excluded) works out to roughly $0.15-0.25 a year (my arithmetic). It is a growth lever the FY27 guide can include.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal day (2026-10-20, with the 8-K item 2.02) moved -0.39% (baseline). The stock rose +1.6% the next day (AAII).
findings.why_not_priced: No accretion figure or FY27 contribution was given on deal day ('more details after close'), so the street's FY27 number may not carry it. The first quantification would come with the guide. Financing question answered: the money buys a growing defense IT business with ~1,100 cleared staff, not a hole. The cost is likely slower buybacks from the unused $400M authorization.
findings.independence: Revenue and margin from Washington Technology (https://www.washingtontechnology.com/companies/2026/10/maximus-seeks-greater-technical-depth-660m-agile-defense-acquisition/416702/). Terms from the 8-K.

findings.finding: The 2026-10-20 8-K (item 2.02) disclosed preliminary net leverage of 1.7x at 2026-09-30, against 2.0x at 2026-06-30 (Q3 release). That implies roughly $200M+ of net debt reduction in Q4 on similar trailing EBITDA. It is consistent with the large Q4 collection the FY26 FCF guide of $425-475M needs after a -$137M Q3, and with the guided DSO under 70 (98 at Q3).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cash/DSO has been a recurring concern (Q3 FCF -$137M, DSO 98). No isolated reaction to a cash beat in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It sat in an acquisition 8-K, framed as pro-forma leverage, and no preview or aggregator carries it as a cash read. It lands inside what the company guided (FCF $425-475M), so it de-risks rather than surprises, and is sized small.
findings.independence: Q3 leverage 2.0x from the Q3 release (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260806885274/en/). DSO and FCF guidance from the Q3 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: the stock went into Q4 beaten down and rallied +5.5% on a below-street guide. This time it goes in after a sharp run, which is a different setup.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The finding is that the run-up raised the bar, not that the run is mispriced. Still -34% from the 52-week high and ~8x FY26 EPS, which caps how much the run-up matters.
findings.independence: AAII October low $52.45 and Oct 21 close $62.07 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/528844-why-maximus-inc8217s-mms-stock-is-down-536). Earnings Whispers +14% since report (https://finviz.com/news/421257/maximus-faces-va-incentive-pause-test-after-cutting-profit-outlook-as-shares-rally).

findings.finding: On 2026-10-29 the D. Mass. court (Massachusetts v. Oz) vacated part of CMS's June 2026 interim final rule on Medicaid community-engagement frailty criteria. It gave 25 plaintiff states plus DC six months of penalty protection, but the Jan 1, 2027 work-requirement start stands. Maximus said in August that prospect talks were progressing 'more slowly than expected', so the court's carve-out may slow the state contracts the FY27 US Services guide counts on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on this line. Medicaid volumes drove the Feb 2026 revenue miss (-16.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: It is policy-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed, so it is a proxy and sized small. The ruling postdates every company statement.
findings.independence: Maximus's 'more slowly than expected' comment on prospects (https://www.webull.com/news/15396980998677504).

findings.finding: Federal FY2027 runs on a continuing resolution at FY26 levels through 2026-12-11 (H.R. 6500, signed 2026-09-02). No appropriation bill is enacted, so Q1 FY27 carries a shutdown or extended-CR risk that management may caveat in the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved print on this line in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: Widely known, so mostly priced. It is filed only because it can shape the guide's caveats. Macro, not confirmed by the company.

findings.why_not_priced: It is positioning, not information. It is filed so judges can weigh squeeze risk on the negatives.
findings.independence: Massive: 3.41M shares, 4.1 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/mms).

findings.finding: Q4 consensus EPS of $1.88 sits below the company-implied $1.91 midpoint, and Q3 beat ($2.22). Base case is an EPS beat or in-line; revenue is expected at the low end of the $5.2-5.35bn FY range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Quarter beats have not set direction for this name: the Q3 beat fell -7.6% on the guide, and the Q4 FY25 miss rose +5.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat against a consensus set below guidance is the base case. It lands inside what the company guided.

baseline_tension: There is no usable skew. The evidence leans mildly against the 20-day run-up (a run-rate guide below street after a ~23% rally), while the cash walk, the acquisition and the contract extension point the other way. Net the lean is small, so p_up sits near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar): the FY27 street number has one 2-analyst source, so the run-rate guide finding was capped from -2.0 to -1.2.
Rule 3 / two readings of one theme: the Leidos 2027 framing partly duplicates the run-rate finding, so it went from -0.8 to -0.5.
Rule 1 (reaction function): this name rallied on a below-street Q4 guide last year, so the run-up/expectations finding went from -1.5 to -1.2 and p_up moved from 45 to 46.
Rule 5 (proxy): the Medicaid court-ruling transmission is unconfirmed by the company, so it went from -0.4 to -0.3.
Rule 8 (thin coverage, first FY27 guide): abs_move_pct raised from 7.5 to 8.0.
Rule 4 (financing): Agile Defense is already signed as a positive after asking what the money buys. Unchanged.
